method.terminal: headed opencode TUI (opencode.exe -s <sid>) on the sandbox host (port 47911, host 2.4.0), launched detached; hosted in a classic console window (conhost.exe, class ConsoleWindowClass). Part 1 (F, command list, /forge stop, anchor) ran on the sandbox host booted 2026-11-24T04:19:04.785Z with production defaults (native-child ceiling 900000, default notice interval); part 2 (stale notice) on a fresh sandbox host started with the 15000 ms notice interval.
method.input: computer-use plugin (opencode-computer-use) -> cua-driver 0.28.2: single-key presses delivered in the BACKGROUND to the sandbox TUI window only (every prompt typed one key at a time: lowercase letters, digits, space, period; the driver delivers shifted symbols unshifted, so no prompt relied on punctuation). Input re-read from a screenshot / zoom crop before every submit. Window close: the driver's UIA click on the window's own Close button. No foreground delivery was used at any point; the user's desktop focus was never taken.
method.observation: driver screenshots after every step + PrintWindow PNG files in logs/ (tui-0340-f1-dialog.png, tui-0340-commands.png, tui-0340-stop.png, tui-0340-stop-final.png, tui-0340-anchor.png, tui-0340-stale.png); ground truth re-read from disk/transcript by tui-postcheck-crew.mjs, tui-postcheck-stop0340.mjs, tui-postcheck-anchor.mjs and tui-postcheck-stale0340.mjs; permission requests observed by tui-askwatch.mjs (500 ms poll of /api/session/<id>/permission)
windowsTouched: pid 42352 hwnd 0x91153a (command list + /forge stop with queued wishes; /new + forge_shell anchor)
method.driverRecovery: the real host's computer-use driver session had been reaped as idle by the cua-driver daemon; recovered by ending the plugin's own dead 'cua-driver.exe mcp' child (pid 38456, child of the real host 35748) so that the plugin restarted its driver and called start_session again — no second driver client was started next to the real host's lease

scopeNotes: F was exercised with 'ws' as the host's last initialized directory (the state in which the confirmation dialog is known to work). The case of a session in a directory that is NOT the last initialized one — the dialog does not pop there — is the known confirmation-door defect; its fix (openspec change fix-ask-door-multi-directory-host, approved by the user on 2026-11-24) is NOT part of 0.34.0 and is NOT covered by this gate.
The '/new' sessions of the A item were created by the TUI itself, after the third directory had become the host's latest initialization.
